title: Exact Microscopic One-Body Reduction in the Symmetric Exclusion Process
abstract: The symmetric exclusion process (SEP) is a paradigmatic model of interacting particle transport. Its current--density correlations are governed by an infinite many-body hierarchy of equations. Only recently, this hierarchy was found to collapse at large scales onto a single closed equation. Is this remarkable simplification created by coarse graining, or does it reflect a deeper property already present in the microscopic dynamics? Here we show that the second scenario is realized. At arbitrary time on the lattice, the entire hierarchy collapses onto a single linear equation which is exactly equivalent to a persistence problem for a single auxiliary random walker. Thus an interacting many-body problem reduces exactly to a genuine one-body problem before any scaling limit is taken. This reduction determines the complete finite-time correlation profile, including during nonequilibrium relaxation. More broadly, the microscopic operator uncovered here opens a route to more general correlation functions in the SEP, and may point to a general organizing principle for nonequilibrium interacting particle systems.
summary: This theoretical paper solves a long-standing problem in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics concerning the Symmetric Exclusion Process (SEP). The authors demonstrate that the complex, infinite-body correlation hierarchy simplifies exactly at the microscopic level, not just in the continuum limit. This reduction maps the interacting system onto a solvable one-body random walker problem, providing exact finite-time correlation profiles.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental question of whether the known large-scale closure of the correlation hierarchy in the Symmetric Exclusion Process (SEP) is an emergent property of coarse-graining or an exact feature of the microscopic dynamics.
main_result: The authors prove that the entire many-body hierarchy collapses exactly onto a single linear equation at arbitrary time, reducing the complex interacting system to an equivalent one-body problem governed by a single auxiliary random walker.
method: The analysis involves extending the Bethe-ansatz calculation using the stirring representation, deriving a closed linear equation for the correlation profile, and mapping this differential equation to a solvable renewal equation.
model_or_system: The system studied is the Symmetric Exclusion Process (SEP), a canonical model for interacting particle transport on a lattice where particles undergo symmetric random walks subject to hard-core exclusion.
key_observables: The correlation profile $\omega_r(t; \lambda)$, which encodes spatial structure associated with current fluctuations, and the $n$-particle propagator $P^{(n)}_t$.
important_parameters: The analysis covers both the finite-time, microscopic regime and the large-scale continuum limit, with the key parameter being time $t$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on adapting techniques from the Bethe ansatz and utilizing complex analysis methods like contour deformation and the Poisson transform.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the SEP as a stirring process, which is central to the mathematical framework used for the derivation.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the correlation profile using determinantal formulas derived from the Bethe ansatz, demonstrating the exact microscopic closure equation, and finally showing that this equation reduces the many-body problem to a single random walker equivalent.
why_interesting: The exact reduction of a complex interacting many-body system to a simple one-body problem provides a powerful, non-perturbative tool for calculating correlation functions in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

A configuration of the SEP is obtained by filling the sites hosting a label that was initially occupied by a particle (blue).
